text:
Elliot: quick recap from the design sync: we need a bounded abstraction for "release grants" that works across hosted/dedicated/private without leaking implementation detail. thinking in terms of three primitives: attest, grant, revoke.
Priya: i like primitives. proposal: grant = opaque short-lived token (JWS) containing scope + min-evidence-hash. runtimes never get raw policy blobs. revoke must be pushable (controlplane -> runtime via long-poll or streaming).
Marco: question on attestation types: hardware attestation, agent-signed key, and proxy-mtls. do we standardize a single verification interface that returns a small enum like {OK, WEAK, UNKNOWN}? avoids propagating complex attestation payloads.
Jules: policy enforcement modes matter a lot for customers. suggest mapping defaults: hosted=ENFORCE, dedicated=ENFORCE|WARN (contract), private=CONFIGURABLE. also add an "emergency-escape" that requires 2-person signoff for operator override.
Elliot: agree. also propose a "signal attenuation" rule: controlplane advertises which signals are authoritative per hosting mode. e.g., hosted authoritative for billing, region; dedicated partial for billing; private only what operator exposes. runtimes must treat non-authoritative signals as untrusted.
Priya: operational nuance: for private offline unlock, support a ciphertext escrow + local decrypt command. operator runs:
```
redwood-escrow unlock --policy pii_block --sign-by ops-team
```
this writes a grant to local broker and records audit entry. no outbound attestation required.
Marco: performance concern: attestation + grant exchange adds latency. our guidance: 1) pre-warm grants on cold-start for hot routes 2) cache per (tenant, model, route) with TTL and explicit invalidation hook on rollout 3) streaming sessions may use a "hot-lease" with heartbeat. quantify defaults in RFC.
Jules: security: keep a short default TTL (e.g., 300s). force re-attestation during model rollout or when sensitive policy changes. rotate broker signing keys regularly and accept old keys for a small grace window.
Elliot: audit model: emit release_event with {policy_id, release_adapter, evidence_hash, release_cid}. telemetry must store no plaintext. create trace corr id linking request -> grant -> release_event.
Priya: compatibility API idea: GET /runtime/available_signals -> [tenant_id, model_meta, route, geo] with validity_ttl. runtime checks this at startup and degrades conservatively if signals missing.
Marco: failure semantics: recommend conservative default = deny for policies marked 'must_guard', else degrade. define three outcomes: ALLOW, DENY, DEGRADE (feature-limited). document mapping and fallback table.
Jules: ops/runbook: steps to debug grant failures: verify broker jwks, check time skew, verify attestor cert chain, inspect evidence_hash mapping in telemetry. include sample cURLs and minimal kafka alerts for repeated failures.
Elliot: implementation note: token payload should include rid=request_id, scope, exp, and evidence_hash. example JWS claims: {"sub":"tenant:acme","scope":"pii_block_v1","exp":1710000000,"rid":"req-123"}. sign with broker key.
Priya: small DSL for policy language only: boolean predicates over signals, no functions or loops. example predicates: in_region("eu"), model_in_list(["redwood-large-v1"]), request_bytes_lt(4096). keep it verifiable.
Marco: testing: add e2e harness that simulates attestor types and a stress test for grant churn to see cache invalidation behavior. include perf targets and histograms for grant latency.
Jules: customer-facing doc: a short table that explains for each hosting mode what guarantees we provide and what customers must configure for private. useful for sales and onboarding.
Elliot: next tasks: Priya write unlock CLI UX + sample audit record, Marco add perf/cache spec and test harness, Jules write runbook and hosting guarantees doc. i'll synthesize into RFC update.
